mainTopic: God sparing מואב and עמון, the reward for refined speech and for hurrying to a מצוה, and רבי מאיר's ruling on damages involving כותים
overview: The amud opens by finishing an אגדה that עולא told to comfort רב שמואל בר יהודה after his daughter died. משה wanted to fight מואב, but הקדוש ברוך הוא spared מואב and עמון because רות המואביה and נעמה העמונית would come from them. From this עולא builds a קל וחומר: if a righteous girl had been meant to bring good into the world, she surely would have lived. רבי יוחנן then teaches that God rewards even refined speech. The proof is that the younger daughter of לוט named her son modestly, so עמון received fuller protection than מואב. רבי יהושע בן קרחה adds that a person should hurry to do a מצוה, since the elder daughter's one-night head start put her descendants into ישראל four generations earlier. The גמרא then turns to הלכה with a ברייתא about oxen of a Jew and a כותי, where רבי מאיר makes a כותי pay full damage even for a תם. A bloodstain משנה shows that רבי מאיר treats כותים as real Jews, so רבי אבהו explains the full payment as a קנס to keep Jews from mixing with them. רבי זירא challenges this from the fine paid for a violated כותית, and אביי begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משה concludes his reasoning that מואב should be attacked
steps.stepSummary: משה רבינו finishes his קל וחומר: if the מדינים, who only came to help מואב, must be attacked, then מואב itself surely should be.
steps.simpleTranslation: מואב itself, all the more so, shouldn't it be attacked?
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the story mid-sentence. משה רבינו finishes his argument that the nation of מואב should be fought against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, משה noted that the תורה commanded war on מדין, even though מדין only came to help מואב. From there he reasons upward: the main troublemaker, מואב, deserves it even more. This reasoning sets up the answer of הקדוש ברוך הוא in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Moabites, the nation of מואב
Themselves
All the more so; the conclusion of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: The Moabites themselves,
is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קל וחומר of משה רבינו, which began earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה reasoned that מואב, the main enemy, should certainly be attacked if its helper מדין was attacked.

steps.title: God explains why מואב and עמון must be spared
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells משה that His plan is different: two good women, רות המואביה and נעמה העמונית, are destined to come from these nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him: What you were thinking is not what I was thinking. I have two good young birds to bring out from them: רות המואביה and נעמה העמונית.
steps.whatsHappening: הקדוש ברוך הוא turns down the reasoning of משה. He explains that מואב and עמון must survive because two special women will come from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's logic only looked at what these nations had done. הקדוש ברוך הוא looks at the future: רות will be an ancestor of דוד המלך, and נעמה will be a mother in the royal line. Because of the good that will come out of them, the nations are not destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: Entered your mind; what you were thinking
Young doves or fledglings; here, a gentle image for good descendants
Ruth the Moabite, ancestor of דוד המלך
Naamah the Ammonite, wife of שלמה המלך

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer becomes the base of the קל וחומר that עולא uses to comfort the mourning father in the next step.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him:
Not as it entered your mind
has it entered My mind;
two good fledglings
phrases.notes: Literally young birds. It is a loving way of saying two good women who will come from these nations.

phrases.english: I have to bring out from them:
Ruth the Moabite
and Naamah the Ammonite.
phrases.notes: נעמה was the mother of רחבעם, the son of שלמה (מלכים א 14:21).

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כְּשֶׁעָלְתָה עַל דַּעְתְּךָ עָלְתָה עַל דַּעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the conclusion of משה's קל וחומר by giving a reason he did not consider.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the practical conclusion that מואב should be destroyed. It does not dispute משה's logic about what מואב did.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: משה looked only at the nation's guilt. He did not account for the righteous descendants who must still come from it.

steps.title: עולא draws a lesson to comfort the mourning father
steps.stepSummary: עולא builds a קל וחומר from the story: if two nations were spared for two good descendants, a righteous girl with good potential would surely have been kept alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a קל וחומר? If, for the sake of two good fledglings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, had pity on two great nations and did not destroy them, then the daughter of my teacher, if she was righteous and fit to have something good come from her, all the more so she would have lived.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings the story back to the reason he told it: to comfort רב שמואל בר יהודה. He uses the story to explain the daughter's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר runs from big to small. Whole nations were spared for the sake of future good, so one righteous girl with good potential would certainly have been spared. Since she was not, her death was not a sign that God ignored her merit. This is meant to accept the loss as God's judgment, not to insult her.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
Had pity, spared
Nations
Righteous, worthy
How much more so

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not saying the girl was wicked. He is explaining that if her survival had been meant to bring good into the world, God would surely have kept her alive, so her death was part of God's plan.
steps.whatToRemember: God spares even whole nations for the sake of the good that will come from them. עולא uses this to show the mourning father that his daughter's death was God's considered judgment.

phrases.english: And are these matters not a קל וחומר?
If for the sake of two good fledglings
the Holy One, Blessed be He, had pity
on two great nations
and did not destroy them,
then the daughter of my teacher,
phrases.notes: This is the daughter of רב שמואל בר יהודה, whom עולא came to comfort.

phrases.english: if she was righteous

phrases.aramaic: וּרְאוּיָה הִיא לָצֵאת מִמֶּנָּה דָּבָר טוֹב,
phrases.english: and fit for something good to come out of her,
how much more so
that she would have lived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the lesson of God's answer to משה to the case of the girl who died.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Her death was not a failure to value her merit. If her life had been meant to bring good into the world, God would have kept her alive.

steps.title: God never withholds the reward of any creature
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא rewards every creature for its good, even for something as small as refined speech.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not withhold the reward of any creature, even the reward for pleasant speech.
steps.whatsHappening: Because מואב and עמון came up, the גמרא now opens a new teaching. It states that no good act, not even a small one, goes unrewarded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מקפח means to cheat someone out of what they deserve. The rule is that God never does this to anyone. It covers even small things like speaking in a refined way. This sets up the next part of the daf, which will show how this applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Withholds, cheats someone out of
Reward of
Creature, person
Pleasant, refined speech

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle of reward: even the smallest good act, such as choosing respectful words, is counted and rewarded.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not withhold
the reward of any creature,
even the reward for pleasant speech.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the mention of מואב and עמון to open a related teaching about divine reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God rewards every creature for every good act, even for refined speech.

steps.title: מואב may not be fought in war, but forced labor is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The elder daughter named her son מואב openly, so her descendants were protected only from war, not from forced labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The elder daughter called her son 'מואב'. So הקדוש ברוך הוא told משה: 'Do not be at enmity with מואב, and do not fight them in war.' Only war is forbidden. You may still force them into labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving רבי יוחנן's rule that refined speech is rewarded. This line sets up the first half of a comparison, and the other daughter comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name מואב openly hints that the child came from her father. The פסוק forbids only war with מואב, so the גמרא reads it as still allowing forced labor. This smaller protection matches the less refined way she spoke.

keyTerms.meaning: The elder daughter of לוט
The name she gave her son, hinting 'from father'
Forced labor
Do not provoke or contend with

phrases.english: For with the elder, who said "Moab",
phrases.notes: She named her son with a name that openly says 'from father', with no attempt to hide it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses:
"Do not be at enmity with Moab,
and do not contend with them in battle".
It is battle that is not allowed,
but forced labor you may impose on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the proof for רבי יוחנן's rule in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that even refined speech is rewarded
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 2:9, which forbids only war with מואב

steps.title: עמון may not be bothered at all, not even with forced labor
steps.stepSummary: The younger daughter named her son בן עמי politely, so her descendants got full protection, even from forced labor.
steps.simpleTranslation: The younger daughter called her son 'בן עמי'. So הקדוש ברוך הוא told משה: 'When you come near the children of עמון, do not harass them and do not provoke them.' That means not at all, not even forced labor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison. The younger daughter spoke more modestly, so her descendants got more protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עמי means only 'son of my people', which does not openly mention the father. The פסוק about עמון leaves out the word 'war', so the גמרא reads it as a complete ban on bothering them. This bigger reward for refined speech proves רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The younger daughter of לוט
'Son of my people', the polite name she gave her son
At all

steps.whatToRemember: מואב: war is forbidden, forced labor is allowed. עמון: nothing at all is allowed. The difference is a reward for the younger daughter's modest words.

phrases.english: The younger, who said "Ben Ami",

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses:
"And when you come near against the children of Ammon,
do not harass them, nor contend with them".
At all, so that even forced labor
you may not impose on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that even refined speech is rewarded
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 2:19, which forbids any harassment of עמון

steps.title: Always hurry to do a מצוה: the elder daughter's head start
steps.stepSummary: Because the elder daughter acted one night earlier, her descendants joined ישראל four generations before the younger daughter's descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן קרחה: A person should always hurry to do a מצוה. The elder daughter went one night before the younger. Because of that, she came into ישראל four generations earlier: עובד, ישי, דוד, and שלמה. The younger daughter's line did not come in until רחבעם, as the פסוק says: 'And his mother's name was נעמה the Ammonite.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about the same two daughters: rushing to do a מצוה brings a reward. The elder's one-night head start earned her four generations of head start in joining ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the elder daughter came מואב, and from מואב came רות. רות's son עובד was followed by ישי, דוד, and שלמה. The younger daughter's line entered ישראל only when שלמה married נעמה העמונית, the mother of רחבעם, four generations after עובד.

keyTerms.meaning: Should hurry, should be first
A מצוה matter
Generations
Son of שלמה, whose mother was נעמה העמונית

steps.whatToRemember: Being first to do a מצוה matters: one night earlier brought four generations of earlier connection to ישראל.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:
A person should always hurry to a מצוה,
for because of one night
by which the elder preceded the younger,
she preceded her by four generations into Israel:
Obed, Yishai, David, and Solomon;
whereas the younger, not until Rehoboam,
as it is written: "And his mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate lesson drawn from the same story of לוט's daughters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always hurry to do a מצוה, as shown by the elder daughter's four-generation head start.

steps.title: A ברייתא on a Jew's ox and a כותי's ox goring each other
steps.stepSummary: A Jew's ox that gores a כותי's ox is exempt. A כותי's ox that gores a Jew's ox pays half damage if it is a תם and full damage if it is a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If a Jew's ox gores a כותי's ox, the owner is exempt. If a כותי's ox gores a Jew's ox: a תם pays half damage, and a מועד pays full damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and brings a ברייתא about damages between a Jew and a כותי. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two directions. When the Jew's ox does the damage, there is no payment. When the כותי's ox does the damage, the usual rules apply: half damage for a תם, full damage for a מועד.

keyTerms.meaning: A כותי (Samaritan)
An ox not known to gore
An ox already warned for goring
Half the cost of the damage
The full cost of the damage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the rule for a regular non-Jew. Here a כותי's תם pays only half damage, just like the usual rule of a תם.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל כּוּתִי – פָּטוּר;
phrases.english: An ox of a Jew that gored the ox of a Samaritan is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל כּוּתִי שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: and one of a Samaritan that gored the ox of a Jew:
if innocuous, he pays half damage,
and if forewarned, he pays full damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל כּוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה about לוט's daughters and opens a new הלכה discussion about damages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew's ox that gores a כותי's ox is exempt. A כותי's ox that gores a Jew's ox pays half damage as a תם and full damage as a מועד.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: A כותי's ox always pays full damage
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר rules that a Jew's ox that gores a כותי's ox is exempt, and a כותי's ox that gores a Jew's ox pays full damage, whether it is a תם or a מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: A Jew's ox that gored a כותי's ox is exempt. A כותי's ox that gored a Jew's ox pays full damage, whether it is a תם or a מועד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second opinion, that of רבי מאיר, about oxen belonging to a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view (step 8) said a כותי's ox pays half if it is a תם and full if it is a מועד, like a Jew. רבי מאיר is stricter: the כותי pays full damage even for a תם. This is the same way the law treats a non-Jew's ox.

keyTerms.meaning: A Samaritan; a member of the nation settled in שומרון whose conversion was questioned
Exempt; does not have to pay
Full damage; paying the whole loss

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is what makes the גמרא wonder about רבי מאיר's view of the status of כותים in general.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל כּוּתִי – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: A Jew's ox that gored a Samaritan's ox: exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל כּוּתִי שֶׁנָּגַח שׁוֹר שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: And a Samaritan's ox that gored a Jew's ox:
whether it is a first-time gorer or a known gorer,
he pays full damage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, stricter opinion on the same case from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, a כותי's ox that gores a Jew's ox pays full damage even when it is a תם.

steps.title: Does רבי מאיר hold כותים are not real converts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי מאיר's ruling means he holds that כותים are גרי אריות, people who converted only out of fear of lions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבי מאיר holds that כותים are גרי אריות, converts out of fear of lions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind רבי מאיר's ruling. This question sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a conversion happened only out of fear, it does not count, so the כותים would be treated like non-Jews. That would explain why רבי מאיר makes them pay full damage like a non-Jew. The גמרא is checking whether this is really his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? The גמרא draws out what a statement seems to imply
Converts out of fear of lions; people whose conversion was forced by fear and so does not count

phrases.english: Is this to say that Rabbi Meir holds:
Samaritans are lion-converts?
phrases.notes: This refers to מלכים ב 17, where the people settled in שומרון were attacked by lions and then took on the worship of ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what reason is behind רבי מאיר's ruling in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי מאיר's ruling based on the view that the conversion of the כותים does not count?

steps.title: Challenge from the law of bloodstains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about bloodstains where רבי מאיר treats the stains of כותים like those of ישראל. That suggests he sees them as real Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: All bloodstains that come from רקם are pure. רבי יהודה says they are impure, because the people there are converts who went astray. Stains from among non-Jews are pure. Stains from among Jews and from among כותים: רבי מאיר says they are impure, and the חכמים say they are pure, because Jews are not suspected of being careless with their stains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that seems to show רבי מאיר holds the opposite: that כותים are real Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stains from non-Jews are pure, because the law of נדה does not apply to them. In this משנה, רבי מאיר puts כותים together with ישראל and rules their stains impure. That means he treats them as true Jews, which goes against the idea from step 10 that he sees them as גרי אריות.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction; the גמרא sets one source against another
Bloodstains found on clothing, which may be impure as נדה blood
Rekem, a city where most people were not Jewish
Converts who went astray; real converts who forgot their Judaism
Rules impure / rule pure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי יהודה's view about Rekem with רבי מאיר's view. The contradiction comes only from the last part, where רבי מאיר groups כותים together with ישראל.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא now needs to explain how רבי מאיר can treat כותים like non-Jews for damages but like Jews for bloodstains.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
All bloodstains that come from Rekem are pure.
Rabbi Yehuda rules them impure,
because they are converts who went astray.
Stains from among non-Jews are pure.
Stains from among Jews and from among Samaritans:
Rabbi Meir rules them impure;
and the Sages rule them pure,
because Jews are not suspected regarding their stains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggestion in step 10 by quoting a source where רבי מאיר seems to treat כותים as real Jews.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי מאיר holds כותים are גרי אריות (step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the law of bloodstains, רבי מאיר treats the stains of כותים like those of ישראל, which only makes sense if they are real Jews. So he cannot hold that their conversion does not count.

steps.title: So רבי מאיר holds that כותים are real converts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the bloodstain משנה: רבי מאיר must hold that כותים are גרי אמת. That clashes with his harsh damages ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that רבי מאיר holds that כותים are true converts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the challenge it started in the last step. It spells out what the bloodstain משנה proves about רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Non-Jews' bloodstains are not טמא at all. So if רבי מאיר treats כותים' stains like Jewish stains, he must see them as full Jews. That makes it hard to explain why he makes their ox pay full damage even when it is a תם, the way a non-Jew's ox would.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out / apparently. Used to draw a conclusion from a source.
He holds (this opinion)
True converts, people who converted sincerely and are full Jews

phrases.english: It turns out that רבי מאיר holds
that כותים are true converts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קשיא of step 11 by stating what the bloodstain משנה proves.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי מאיר's full-damages ruling (step 9) comes from seeing כותים as גרי אריות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere רבי מאיר treats כותים as full Jews, so his damages ruling cannot be based on their being non-Jews.

steps.title: It is a fine so Jews will not mix with them
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers: כותים really are Jews, but רבי מאיר fined them with money so that Jews would not mix with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is a fine that רבי מאיר placed on their money, so that people will not mix with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו settles the contradiction. רבי מאיר does hold that כותים are real Jews, but in money matters he made a special penalty for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to Torah law, a כותי's תם ox should pay only half damage, like any Jew's. רבי מאיר added a קנס so they pay full damage, which keeps a distance between Jews and כותים. So the bloodstain law follows their true status, and the damages law is a rabbinic penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine or penalty added by the חכמים
Their money
Become mixed in, assimilate

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אבהו is calling כותים non-Jews. He says they ARE Jews; the full payment is only an extra penalty.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates a group's real status from a penalty the חכמים placed on them, and the rest of the discussion tests that idea.

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said:

phrases.aramaic: קְנָס הוּא שֶׁקָּנַס רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמָמוֹנָם,
phrases.english: It is a fine that רבי מאיר imposed on their money,
so that people will not mix in with them.
phrases.notes: He means Jews should not get too close to the כותים and marry into them.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְנָס הוּא שֶׁקָּנַס רַבִּי מֵאִיר בְּמָמוֹנָם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the ruling: it is a rabbinic קנס, not a statement about their status.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's full-damages ruling shows he sees כותים as non-Jews.
steps.terutzMaskana: כותים are real Jews. The full payment is a קנס to keep Jews from mixing with them.

steps.title: Then why not also fine the כותית girl?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes a משנה that a man who violates a כותית girl must pay the fine to her father. If רבי מאיר fines כותים, why not take away this payment too?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: These are the girls who receive a fine: one who has relations with a ממזרת, a נתינה, or a כותית. If you think רבי מאיר fined their money, here too let us fine them so people will not mix with them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רבי אבהו's answer from a משנה about girls who are violated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the man pays the fine even when the girl is a כותית, so she is treated like any Jewish girl. If רבי מאיר wanted to penalize כותים in money matters, this would be an obvious place to do it by taking the payment away. Since the משנה does not do that, רבי אבהו's idea of a קנס looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Young girls (between about 12 and 12½)
A girl born from a forbidden relationship
A girl from the גבעונים, who are forbidden to marry into ישראל
A כותי girl
If you think / if it enters your mind

phrases.english: רבי זירא raised an objection:
And these are the girls who receive a fine:
one who has relations with a ממזרת,
or with a נתינה, or with a כותית.
And if you think
that רבי מאיר fined their money,
then here too let us fine them,
phrases.notes: He means: take away the payment the כותית's father would get.

phrases.english: so that people will not mix in with them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אבהו's תירוץ in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that רבי מאיר fined כותים in money matters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason to fine them, keeping Jews from mixing with them, applies to the כותית's rape payment. Yet the משנה still gives her the payment.

steps.title: אביי begins to answer
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to explain why no fine was placed in the case of the כותית girl. His answer continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening of אביי's answer. The גמרא is setting up his explanation of why the כותית case is different, and it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כדי ('in order') tells us אביי will give a reason why the חכמים chose not to fine in this case. So far we only know that he is defending רבי אבהו's idea of a קנס against רבי זירא.

keyTerms.meaning: In order that; it introduces a reason

phrases.english: אביי said: In order
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here. The rest of אביי's reason comes at the start of the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering רבי זירא's קשיא in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason the חכמים did not fine in this case (answer continues).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If כותים are fined, the כותית should lose her payment too.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a special reason not to fine here. The details continue on the next amud.
